1	---
2	name: horizon-inbox
3	description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
4	---
5	
6	The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
7	future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
8	by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
9	fields.
10	
11	## Read
12	
13	- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
14	  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
15	  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
16	  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
17	  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
18	- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
19	  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
20	  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
21	  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
22	- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
23	  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
24	- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
25	  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
26	  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
27	  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
28	  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
29	- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
30	  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
31	  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
32	  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
33	  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
34	  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
35	- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
36	  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
37	  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
38	  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
39	  Scope/project says what the item is about.
40	- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
41	  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
42	  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
43	- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
44	  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
45	  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
46	  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
47	- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
48	  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
49	  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
50	  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
51	  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
52	  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).
53	
54	## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)
55	
56	Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
57	lightweight overlays keep it navigable:
58	
59	- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
60	  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
61	  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
62	  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
63	  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
64	  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
65	  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
66	- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
67	  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
68	  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
69	  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
70	  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
71	  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.
72	
73	Read in this order before editing:
74	
75	1. `horizon inbox list --mine --status open --kind protection --json` — every
76	   active protection is required even if your team previously marked it read.
77	2. `horizon inbox list --mine --unread --kind conversation --json` — open each
78	   result with `inbox show`; reply when a response is needed, otherwise the read
79	   acknowledgement clears it until another participant replies.
80	3. Consult hint/issue/info/memory items as advisory context for the task.
81	
82	The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
83	it explicitly.
84	
85	## Act
86	
87	Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
88	attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
89	**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
90	`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
91	If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
92	work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
93	next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
94	comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
95	UI); you do not pass this yourself.
96	
97	New inbox items use a two-part body:
98	
99	- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
100	  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
101	- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
102	  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
103	  item that is only a title is rejected.
104	
105	Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Use short
106	paragraphs and `-` bullet lists instead of one wall-of-text paragraph, `**bold**`
107	for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, files, and code
108	(`` `lem:foo` ``, `` `Foo.lean:42` ``). For a multi-part result, start with a
109	one-sentence conclusion, then use `## Result`, `## Evidence`, `## Impact`, and
110	`## Next action` as applicable; omit empty sections. The CLI rejects long new
111	agent descriptions, opening messages, and comments with no paragraph, heading,
112	or list structure.
113	
114	Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
115	`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
116	of that paragraph concise.
117	
118	Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
119	`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
120	`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
121	open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
122	main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
123	solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
124	obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.
125	
126	### Conversation lifecycle
127	
128	A conversation is for an expected reply, decision, or active coordination. A
129	one-way handoff or announcement is an `info`/`hint`, not a conversation.
130	
131	1. **Search before starting:** inspect open conversations for the same topic and
132	   participants (`inbox list --status open --kind conversation --query "key words"
133	   --json`). Reply to the existing thread whenever it can carry the update. Do not
134	   open one thread per incremental finding.
135	2. **One question, one thread:** keep follow-ups, answers, corrections, and the
136	   final decision as comments on that thread. Start another only when it has a
137	   genuinely different decision boundary or participant set.
138	3. **Answer before branching:** when a conversation becomes unread, open it and
139	   answer or acknowledge it before starting another conversation with the same
140	   team.
141	4. **The initiator closes:** if `metadata.started_by` is your task/run, you own
142	   the lifecycle. Once the requested answer has arrived and been consumed, add a
143	   short conclusion comment when the outcome is not obvious, then
144	   `horizon inbox archive <id>`. Do this during the session, not only after a
145	   warning says the inbox is full.
146	5. **Do not hide an answer from its initiator:** recipients normally reply and
147	   leave closure to the initiator. For a human-started thread, answer it but leave
148	   it open for the human to consume/archive unless the human explicitly delegates
149	   closure. Use `complete` instead of `archive` only when the concluded thread is
150	   intentionally meant to remain visible in the resolved working record.
151	6. **End-of-session sweep:** before the final report, inspect open conversations
152	   in which your task is `started_by`. Archive every resolved one and state a real
153	   blocker on any that must remain open. An accumulation of open conversations is
154	   unfinished coordination, not harmless history.
155	
156	- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
157	  what you did; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
158	  into the comment body; the author is set automatically. Drop a comment at each **key advance**
159	  while you work an item (a milestone reached, a route ruled out, a blocker hit),
160	  not only at the end — these comments are the item's visible progress trail.
161	- `horizon inbox dm task:<id> [task:<id> ...] --body "Topic\n\nOpening message"`
162	  — start a one-to-one or group conversation. Use `horizon ps` to discover live
163	  teams. Use it only after the lifecycle search above. The sender remains a
164	  participant and owns closure; every reply makes the thread unread for the other
165	  participants. Humans read and reply from the live dashboard.
166	- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
167	  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
168	  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
169	  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
170	  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
171	  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
172	  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
173	- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
174	  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
175	  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
176	  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
177	  For a conversation you initiated, this is the normal "discussion finished"
178	  operation after its answer/conclusion has been consumed.
179	- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
180	  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
181	  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
182	  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
183	  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
184	  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
185	- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
186	  — open a new item.
187	  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct
188	    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.
189	    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
190	    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it"); use `--to task:<id>` to
191	    message a specific running team.
192	  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
193	    the shared default.
194	  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
195	  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
196	    tag to the body.
197	  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
198	    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
199	- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
200	  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
201	  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
202	- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
203	  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
204	  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
205	  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
206	  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
207	  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.
208	
209	Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
210	it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
211	one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
212	modified.

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	Two of the committed route's own engines are substantially built.  The rigidified
21	pushforward gate is **discharged**: `Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve` is a real
22	instance for every curve satisfying the challenge hypotheses, and it measures axiom-clean
23	at the synthesis site, as do the three extraction theorems that now synthesise it rather
24	than assuming it.  The finite Galois
25	quotient has Speiser descent, the affine quotient, and `Γ`-stable affine covers proved;
26	what remains there is gluing.  Both are stated with proofs and Lean pins in the
27	blueprint's FGA chapter, §"The Milne–Kollár route".  Neither route is hypothesis-free:
28	the quotient route needs quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice, the committed route
29	needs every finite Galois orbit to lie in an affine open, and the same Hironaka example
30	defeats both if its hypothesis is dropped.  The difference is that the orbit condition is
31	available for the schemes this route quotients.
32	
33	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
34	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
35	
36	## State (measured 2026-07-28)
37	
38	- **202 modules, 137,433 lines**; **28 `sorry`** over 11 modules, the rest locally
39	  sorry-free; a warm `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **green** at 8,746 jobs (job count last
40	  measured before the 2026-07-28 lanes landed).  These counts move whenever a module lands, and
41	  four AJC lanes were live when they were taken, so re-measure rather than quoting them:
42	
43	  ```bash
44	  find AlgebraicJacobian -name '*.lean' | wc -l          # modules on disk
45	  find AlgebraicJacobian -name '*.lean' -exec cat {} + | wc -l
46	  lake build AlgebraicJacobian 2>&1 | grep -c 'declaration uses .sorry'
47	  ```
48	- **Rootedness is worth measuring, not assuming.**  A module that nothing imports
49	  compiles green and is invisible *both* to the root build and to the axiom probe,
50	  with nothing warning about it — `import AlgebraicJacobian` never reaches it, so no
51	  `#print axioms` line for it can even be written.  The check is the second
52	  measurement in [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean)'s
53	  header.  Modules land here from several parallel efforts, so the unrooted set is
54	  routinely non-empty for a short while: a module not yet committed to the workspace
55	  ledger must **not** be rooted, since a clean checkout would then fail to build.  That
56	  grace period ends at the commit — once a module is in the ledger, leaving it unrooted
57	  means the build does not check it.
58	- **Locally sorry-free is not axiom-clean.**  Two `sorry`-bodied *instances* leak
59	  through typeclass synthesis: `instHasPicScheme`
60	  (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the sole producer of `HasPicScheme`) and
61	  `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
62	  (`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`).  A theorem that merely
63	  *quantifies over* such a gate reports clean axioms, because the hypothesis is
64	  discharged by the caller; the leak appears at any call site that must
65	  synthesise the instance.  Run
66	  [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean) (`lake env lean
67	  scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`, 147 declarations: 95 clean and 52 carrying `sorryAx`,
68	  measured 2026-07-28 with `lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian` green at 8,657
69	  jobs) before believing any
70	  completeness claim — it measures the frontier rather than inferring it.  Count by
71	  output *entry*, not by output line:
72	  Lean wraps a long axiom list across several lines, so a per-line filter
73	  misclassifies exactly the declarations with the longest lists.  The header carries
74	  the recipe.
75	- **A clean axiom set answers one question only:** is a `sorry` reachable from this
76	  proof term.  Eight separate things it cannot see have each been found in this
77	  tree — a `sorry`-bodied instance reached only through synthesis; an *unproved*
78	  named hypothesis in the statement; a *false* named hypothesis in the statement,
79	  which makes the theorem vacuously true and perfectly clean; an
80	  *un-instantiable instance binder*, where the obligation sits in square brackets
81	  and nothing in the project constructs it for the ambient object actually used
82	  (an instance for a more structured cousin — `Over (Spec k)` rather than a bare
83	  `Scheme` — does not count, and is worse than none, because the grep succeeds);
84	  an *unrooted module*, which no axiom check reaches at all, per the bullet
85	  above; and an *instance diamond*, where two non-definitionally-equal instances can
86	  supply the same binder, so a file can prove correct-looking theorems about a
87	  definition pinned to the wrong one; and a *refutable* hypothesis, whose negation the
88	  tree already derives at every instance anyone would use, so the project proves both
89	  `H → C` and `¬H` and the theorem is true, clean, consistent, instantiable and empty.
90	  The first five are each measured by the probe; the sixth defeats the probe *and* an
91	  instantiability check, because the binders do synthesise — the tell is a cross-file
92	  identity that ought to be `rfl` and is not.  The seventh defeats every check in this
93	  file including a consistency witness: the only thing that finds it is reading the
94	  *producer's* side conditions and asking where the family the hypothesis quantifies
95	  over contains a member whose negation the tree proves (measured on the χ-ledger's
96	  `hbump`, probe §2b).  The eighth is the cheapest to check and worth checking first: a
97	  hypothesis *equivalent* to the conclusion it is supposed to buy, so that `H → C` is a
98	  restatement rather than a reduction — try to prove `C → H` before believing the
99	  reduction (probe §2c).  Read the probe's section headers, not just its output lines.
100	- **Only two of the tree's `sorry` carriers are instances**, and that is the whole of
101	  the synthesis-leak surface, because an instance is the only carrier a consumer can
102	  reach without naming it.  The probe's §2 lists all 26 carriers by module (the two
103	  instances plus 24 theorems and definitions), so the claim is checkable rather than
104	  folklore; note that two of those 24 hold their `sorry` in a *field*, which a grep
105	  for `:= sorry` misses.  Re-derive rather than trust the number:
106	
107	  ```bash
108	  lake build AlgebraicJacobian 2>&1 | grep 'declaration uses' | sort -u
109	  ```
110	- 66 modules still open with a bare `import Mathlib`; this is the
111	  dominant build cost and is being converted bottom-up with the helpers in
112	  `scripts/`.
113	
114	## Decision made: the headline is stated over an arbitrary field
115	
116	**Settled 2026-07-28 by the project owner** (roadmap `AJC.picrep.rational-point`,
117	inbox `I-0372`, protection `I-0491`).  The Jacobian headline is stated over an
118	**arbitrary** base field with **no** rational-point hypothesis, and what gets
119	represented is the **étale-sheafified** relative Picard functor.  This is Kleiman's
120	own formulation and the full strength the challenge asks for.  It is not a branch to
121	revisit.
122	
123	What that means concretely, and each piece is checkable:
124	
125	- `Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` builds the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
126	  `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and **proves its sheaf property** (`picEt_isSheaf_forget`) — it is
127	  a sheafification, so the axiom holds by construction rather than by hypothesis.  The
128	  étale site is Mathlib v4.31's `Scheme.etaleTopology` localised at `Spec k` along
129	  SGA 4 III 5.2.1.  The file is `sorry`-free.
130	- `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) is the
131	  representability obligation, restated for that functor with no rational point.  It
132	  is **one named `sorry`** and is the project's central open obligation; it is
133	  expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.
134	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` has been **deleted**.  It asserted a `k`-rational point
135	  from the challenge hypotheses alone, which is *false* — a conic over `ℚ` without
136	  rational points, or a genus-2 curve over `ℚ` without one, satisfies every other
137	  hypothesis.  While it existed the witness rested on an inconsistent hypothesis, so
138	  its consequences were vacuously true and no axiom check could tell.  It must never
139	  be proved or reinstated.
140	- `picardJacobianWitness` now carries exactly the three challenge hypotheses
141	  (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsProper`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`) and nothing
142	  else.  This is checked, not asserted: `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` has a
143	  `HeadlineBinders` section whose `example`s stop elaborating if a
144	  `[HasRationalPoint _]` binder ever returns to the headline cone.
145	
146	**The obligation count is unchanged at five, and that is the deliverable.**  The
147	witness rests on `fgaPicardRepresentability`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced`,
148	`Pic0Et.universallyClosed`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` and

150	over the middle two, so citing them as the open statements is a stale reading.)  What changed is not
151	the number but the *kind*: **none of the five is a false statement any more**.  All
152	five are true statements awaiting proofs.  That difference is invisible to
153	`#print axioms` — it is a property of the statements, not of the proof terms — which
154	is why it is argued at the binders instead.
155	
156	Two things are kept beside the headline and **neither may be presented as it**:
157	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, an explicitly *conditional* milestone

159	`picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`, a genuine theorem over `k̄`.  The

161	but it is **no longer an instance**: its only producer is the named theorem
162	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so nothing picks up a rational-point hypothesis by

164	
165	The route choice is unaffected: Milne–Kollár stays committed, Quot stays
166	retained-not-revived.
167	
168	
169	Cones closed: `AJC.substrate`, `AJC.linebundle`, `AJC.grquot`, `AJC.cech`.

178	- [`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean): the final

1	# LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
2	
3	LeanAG Horizon is a multi-project Lean 4 and Mathlib workspace for formalizing algebraic
4	geometry with [Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon). Its central goal is
5	the algebraic-geometry version of the [Algebraic Jacobian challenge](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/583336-Autoformalization/topic/Jacobian.20challenge/near/587802685),
6	proposed by Christian Merten after Kevin Buzzard's differential-geometry challenge.
7	
8	> [!IMPORTANT]
9	> The workspace develops **two live routes** to the Algebraic Jacobian challenge. Follow the
10	> project named by the active task rather than treating either route as reference-only.
11	>
12	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` continues the ambitious Picard-scheme route, building
13	>   representability by the Milne–Kollár construction of `Pic^r`, then `Pic^0` and the Albanese
14	>   property. Its Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening-stratification substrate is sorry-free
15	>   and still consumed, but the Quot-scheme endgame it was first written for is not the path being
16	>   built. Since 2026-07-28 its headline is stated over an arbitrary base field, with
17	>   representability asked of the étale-sheafified Picard functor and no rational-point hypothesis.
18	> - `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` develops a cleaner curve-specialized route
19	>   from protected target statements.
20	
21	The two projects share mathematical sources and supporting subprojects while keeping independent
22	Lean roots, blueprints, and roadmaps. The rebuild is listed first in the workspace manifest as the
23	default project; explicitly scoped tasks may and do advance the ambitious original route.
24	
25	The [live dashboard](https://axeldlv00.github.io/LeanAlgebraicGeometry/) is the best view of current
26	tasks, commits, session logs, blueprint graphs, and declaration-level progress. A static snapshot
27	is published approximately every 30 minutes; GitHub Pages deployment and caching can add a few
28	minutes before a new snapshot is visible.
29	
30	## Repository Layout
31	
32	| Path | Role |
33	| --- | --- |
34	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` | Cleaner curve-specialized AJC route and workspace default. |
35	| `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme AJC route (Milne–Kollár representability), maintained by scoped tasks. |
36	| `SubProjects/` | Supporting, extracted, and related-paper formalizations available to the active project. |
37	| `references/` | Shared mathematical sources and retrieval notes. |
38	| `.archon-horizon/` | Workspace state: tasks, roadmap, inbox, run metadata, graphs, and ledger. |
39	| `config.yaml` | Ordered workspace manifest. The rebuild is listed first because it is the primary project. |
40	
41	Each route has its own overview:
42	
43	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/README.md)
44	- [`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md)
45	
46	## Project Map
47	
48	The workspace currently registers these projects, in priority order:
49	
50	| Project | Purpose |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| **`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`** | Cleaner curve-specialized route; default project in the workspace manifest. |
53	| `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` | Ambitious Picard-scheme, `Pic^0`, and Albanese route. |
54	| `Line-Bundle-Comparison-Iso` | Extracted line-bundle pullback, tensor, and dual comparison infrastructure. |
55	| `Albanese` | Albanese universal property, rigidity, and rational-map-extension infrastructure. |
56	| `Cech-Cohomology` | Čech computation of higher direct images and its cohomological substrate. |
57	| `GR-Quot-Closure` | Relative Grassmannian and quotient-representability infrastructure. |
58	| `MR0555258-Compactifying-Picard` | Compactifying the Picard scheme (D'Souza), under `SubProjects/RelatedPapersFormalisation/`. |
59	| `Picard-IdentityComponent` | Extracted Picard identity-component and `Pic^0` development. |
60	
61	These member projects remain useful sources of proved APIs, mathematical designs, and failure
62	memory for both main routes.
63	
64	## Working in a Main Project
65	
66	The workspace currently uses Lean and Mathlib `v4.31.0`. Build the project named by the task. For
67	the ambitious Picard-scheme route:
68	
69	```bash
70	cd MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge
71	lake build
72	```
73	
74	The rebuild uses the shared workspace package directory at `.lake-packages`, so member projects
75	can reuse the same Mathlib checkout while retaining independent build directories.
76	
77	For workspace-wide exploration, run commands from the repository root:
78	
79	```bash
80	horizon dashboard
81	horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier
82	horizon search "Jacobian Picard representability"
83	```
84	
85	The first command starts the local dashboard. The graph command shows the ranked proof frontier
86	for the active project, and search queries declarations across the workspace and Mathlib.
87	
88	## Methodology
89	
90	[Archon Horizon](https://github.com/frenzymath/Archon-Horizon) coordinates long-running
91	formalization while keeping mathematical and operational state explicit:
92	
93	- **Horizon sessions** implement and verify Lean proofs against concrete tasks.
94	- **Fresh-context reviewers** such as Ground, work-reviewer, and janitor are dispatched at review
95	  and maintenance checkpoints rather than acting as a permanent second driver.
96	- **Blueprint graphs (`hgraph`)** track declaration dependencies, proof status, comments, and the
97	  ranked frontier for each project.
98	- **Roadmap, tasks, and inbox** record strategy, scoped work, cross-session handoffs, and durable
99	  failure memory.
100	- **The workspace ledger** records coherent commits and powers the public dashboard's progress
101	  and session views.
102	
103	Concurrent sessions can share a project's root import file. When adding one
104	import, build the staged root from the ledger's current `HEAD` and insert only
105	that line; do not stage the whole on-disk root, which may contain another
106	session's uncommitted imports.
107	
108	The mathematical blueprint is kept separate from implementation journals. Lean-specific progress
109	and failed approaches belong in graph comments, tasks, or the inbox, while the blueprint remains a
110	timeless account of the mathematics.
111	
112	## Contributing
113	
114	Contributions are welcome, but keep the two routes and task scope explicit:
115	
116	- **AJC proofs and infrastructure:** change only the main project named by the task; share reusable
117	  inputs through the supporting projects when appropriate.
118	- **Protected statements:** do not alter the signatures in the rebuild's `Challenge.lean` or files
119	  covered by `archon-protected.yaml` without prior agreement. Contributions should discharge those
120	  statements, not weaken or reshape them silently.
121	- **Issues and discussions:** include the declaration name and file path, and state whether the
122	  question concerns the statement, naming, proof strategy, or intended use.
123	- **Large changes:** check the live dashboard or open an issue first so work does not duplicate an
124	  active Horizon task.
125	- **Supporting work:** a focused subproject under `SubProjects/` is appropriate when a reusable
126	  dependency needs to be developed independently, but its intended consumer should be the active
127	  rebuild.
128	
129	Clear, stable, mathematical declaration names and warning-free builds are expected. Using the
130	`horizon` CLI is recommended so contributions remain aligned with the workspace manifest,

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	Two of the committed route's own engines are substantially built.  The rigidified
21	pushforward gate is **discharged**: `Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve` is a real
22	instance for every curve satisfying the challenge hypotheses, and it measures axiom-clean
23	at the synthesis site, as do the three extraction theorems that now synthesise it rather
24	than assuming it.  The finite Galois
25	quotient has Speiser descent, the affine quotient, and `Γ`-stable affine covers proved;
26	what remains there is gluing.  Both are stated with proofs and Lean pins in the
27	blueprint's FGA chapter, §"The Milne–Kollár route".  Neither route is hypothesis-free:
28	the quotient route needs quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice, the committed route
29	needs every finite Galois orbit to lie in an affine open, and the same Hironaka example
30	defeats both if its hypothesis is dropped.  The difference is that the orbit condition is
31	available for the schemes this route quotients.
32	
33	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
34	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
35	
36	## State (measured 2026-07-28)
37	
38	- **202 modules, 137,433 lines**; **28 `sorry`** over 11 modules, the rest locally
39	  sorry-free; a warm `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **green** at 8,746 jobs (job count last
40	  measured before the 2026-07-28 lanes landed).  These counts move whenever a module lands, and
41	  four AJC lanes were live when they were taken, so re-measure rather than quoting them:
42	
43	  ```bash
44	  find AlgebraicJacobian -name '*.lean' | wc -l          # modules on disk
45	  find AlgebraicJacobian -name '*.lean' -exec cat {} + | wc -l
46	  lake build AlgebraicJacobian 2>&1 | grep -c 'declaration uses .sorry'
47	  ```
48	- **Rootedness is worth measuring, not assuming.**  A module that nothing imports
49	  compiles green and is invisible *both* to the root build and to the axiom probe,
50	  with nothing warning about it — `import AlgebraicJacobian` never reaches it, so no
51	  `#print axioms` line for it can even be written.  The check is the second
52	  measurement in [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean)'s
53	  header.  Modules land here from several parallel efforts, so the unrooted set is
54	  routinely non-empty for a short while: a module not yet committed to the workspace
55	  ledger must **not** be rooted, since a clean checkout would then fail to build.  That
56	  grace period ends at the commit — once a module is in the ledger, leaving it unrooted
57	  means the build does not check it.
58	- **Locally sorry-free is not axiom-clean.**  Two `sorry`-bodied *instances* leak
59	  through typeclass synthesis: `instHasPicScheme`
60	  (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the sole producer of `HasPicScheme`) and
61	  `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
62	  (`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`).  A theorem that merely
63	  *quantifies over* such a gate reports clean axioms, because the hypothesis is
64	  discharged by the caller; the leak appears at any call site that must
65	  synthesise the instance.  Run
66	  [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean) (`lake env lean
67	  scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`, 147 declarations: 95 clean and 52 carrying `sorryAx`,
68	  measured 2026-07-28 with `lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Jacobian` green at 8,657
69	  jobs) before believing any
70	  completeness claim — it measures the frontier rather than inferring it.  Count by
71	  output *entry*, not by output line:
72	  Lean wraps a long axiom list across several lines, so a per-line filter
73	  misclassifies exactly the declarations with the longest lists.  The header carries
74	  the recipe.
75	- **A clean axiom set answers one question only:** is a `sorry` reachable from this
76	  proof term.  Eight separate things it cannot see have each been found in this
77	  tree — a `sorry`-bodied instance reached only through synthesis; an *unproved*
78	  named hypothesis in the statement; a *false* named hypothesis in the statement,
79	  which makes the theorem vacuously true and perfectly clean; an
80	  *un-instantiable instance binder*, where the obligation sits in square brackets
81	  and nothing in the project constructs it for the ambient object actually used
82	  (an instance for a more structured cousin — `Over (Spec k)` rather than a bare
83	  `Scheme` — does not count, and is worse than none, because the grep succeeds);
84	  an *unrooted module*, which no axiom check reaches at all, per the bullet
85	  above; and an *instance diamond*, where two non-definitionally-equal instances can
86	  supply the same binder, so a file can prove correct-looking theorems about a
87	  definition pinned to the wrong one; and a *refutable* hypothesis, whose negation the
88	  tree already derives at every instance anyone would use, so the project proves both
89	  `H → C` and `¬H` and the theorem is true, clean, consistent, instantiable and empty.
90	  The first five are each measured by the probe; the sixth defeats the probe *and* an
91	  instantiability check, because the binders do synthesise — the tell is a cross-file
92	  identity that ought to be `rfl` and is not.  The seventh defeats every check in this
93	  file including a consistency witness: the only thing that finds it is reading the
94	  *producer's* side conditions and asking where the family the hypothesis quantifies
95	  over contains a member whose negation the tree proves (measured on the χ-ledger's
96	  `hbump`, probe §2b).  The eighth is the cheapest to check and worth checking first: a
97	  hypothesis *equivalent* to the conclusion it is supposed to buy, so that `H → C` is a
98	  restatement rather than a reduction — try to prove `C → H` before believing the
99	  reduction (probe §2c).  Read the probe's section headers, not just its output lines.
100	- **Only two of the tree's `sorry` carriers are instances**, and that is the whole of
101	  the synthesis-leak surface, because an instance is the only carrier a consumer can
102	  reach without naming it.  The probe's §2 lists all 26 carriers by module (the two
103	  instances plus 24 theorems and definitions), so the claim is checkable rather than
104	  folklore; note that two of those 24 hold their `sorry` in a *field*, which a grep
105	  for `:= sorry` misses.  Re-derive rather than trust the number:
106	
107	  ```bash
108	  lake build AlgebraicJacobian 2>&1 | grep 'declaration uses' | sort -u
109	  ```
110	- 66 modules still open with a bare `import Mathlib`; this is the
111	  dominant build cost and is being converted bottom-up with the helpers in
112	  `scripts/`.
113	
114	## Decision made: the headline is stated over an arbitrary field
115	
116	**Settled 2026-07-28 by the project owner** (roadmap `AJC.picrep.rational-point`,
117	inbox `I-0372`, protection `I-0491`).  The Jacobian headline is stated over an
118	**arbitrary** base field with **no** rational-point hypothesis, and what gets
119	represented is the **étale-sheafified** relative Picard functor.  This is Kleiman's
120	own formulation and the full strength the challenge asks for.  It is not a branch to
121	revisit.
122	
123	What that means concretely, and each piece is checkable:
124	
125	- `Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` builds the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
126	  `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and **proves its sheaf property** (`picEt_isSheaf_forget`) — it is
127	  a sheafification, so the axiom holds by construction rather than by hypothesis.  The
128	  étale site is Mathlib v4.31's `Scheme.etaleTopology` localised at `Spec k` along
129	  SGA 4 III 5.2.1.  The file is `sorry`-free.
130	- `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) is the
131	  representability obligation, restated for that functor with no rational point.  It
132	  is **one named `sorry`** and is the project's central open obligation; it is
133	  expected to stay open, and that is the honest state rather than a defect.
134	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` has been **deleted**.  It asserted a `k`-rational point
135	  from the challenge hypotheses alone, which is *false* — a conic over `ℚ` without
136	  rational points, or a genus-2 curve over `ℚ` without one, satisfies every other
137	  hypothesis.  While it existed the witness rested on an inconsistent hypothesis, so
138	  its consequences were vacuously true and no axiom check could tell.  It must never
139	  be proved or reinstated.
140	- `picardJacobianWitness` now carries exactly the three challenge hypotheses
141	  (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`, `IsProper`, `GeometricallyIrreducible`) and nothing
142	  else.  This is checked, not asserted: `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` has a
143	  `HeadlineBinders` section whose `example`s stop elaborating if a
144	  `[HasRationalPoint _]` binder ever returns to the headline cone.
145	
146	**The obligation count is unchanged at five, and that is the deliverable.**  The
147	witness rests on `fgaPicardRepresentability`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced`,
148	`Pic0Et.universallyClosed`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` and
149	`isAlbanese_pic0Et`.  (Not `Pic0Et.smooth` / `Pic0Et.proper`: those are *assemblies*
150	over the middle two, so citing them as the open statements is a stale reading.)  What changed is not
151	the number but the *kind*: **none of the five is a false statement any more**.  All
152	five are true statements awaiting proofs.  That difference is invisible to
153	`#print axioms` — it is a property of the statements, not of the proof terms — which
154	is why it is argued at the binders instead.
155	
156	Two things are kept beside the headline and **neither may be presented as it**:
157	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, an explicitly *conditional* milestone
158	(true under a section, strictly weaker than the challenge), and
159	`picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`, a genuine theorem over `k̄`.  The
160	`picSharp`-shaped gate `HasPicScheme` survives for the consumers written against it,
161	but it is **no longer an instance**: its only producer is the named theorem
162	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so nothing picks up a rational-point hypothesis by
163	synthesis.
164	
165	The route choice is unaffected: Milne–Kollár stays committed, Quot stays
166	retained-not-revived.
167	
168	
169	Cones closed: `AJC.substrate`, `AJC.linebundle`, `AJC.grquot`, `AJC.cech`.
170	Cones open: `AJC.fbc` (flat base change, three leaves), `AJC.rr`, `AJC.picrep`
171	(Picard representability), `AJC.pic0av` (Pic⁰ is an abelian variety),
172	`AJC.albanese`.  Run `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.jacobian` for the live tree
173	— the roadmap, not this file, is the authority on status.
174	
175	## Navigation
176	
177	- [`AlgebraicJacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian.lean): project import root.
178	- [`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean): the final
179	  Jacobian witness interface and assembly point.  The witness is built from
180	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` in its étale form (`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`) and carries **no**
181	  rational-point hypothesis.  It depends on five stated obligations:
182	  `fgaPicardRepresentability` (the representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`),
183	  `Pic0Et.smooth` and `Pic0Et.proper` upstream, plus the two leaves
184	  `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` and `isAlbanese_pic0Et` stated there.  All
185	  five are **true** statements awaiting proofs.  The two leaves carry *companions*
186	  stating what the landed development already reaches
187	  (`finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus`, `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`), so each
188	  leaf's remaining distance is compiler-checked rather than described in prose; both
189	  companions record a distance and carry `sorryAx`, and the probe's §0 says why.
190	- [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean): the axiom-frontier
191	  probe, and the three companion measurements in its header: reachability of the
192	  headline cone, whether every module on disk is rooted at all, and whether every
193	  blueprint proof-level `\leanok` is honest.  The last has to be a `#print axioms` join
194	  rather than a reading pass, because a `\leanok` is a local mark while the defect is
195	  transitive — a proof written in Lean is still not proved if it routes through a `sorry`.
196	  The `\leanok` join is executable — `scripts/leanok-audit.sh`, one command from the
197	  project root, exiting non-zero if any of its three checks fails (the reconciliation
198	  identity on each mark position, plus a positive control proving the `private` lane
199	  still bites).  Run it rather than re-transcribing it: every wrong number this check has
200	  published came from a recipe copied out of a comment and drifting from the code that
201	  produced it.
202	
203	  Current result, both mark positions under the same reconciliation identity:
204	  **proof-level, 1073 pinned declarations across 1078 marks = 930 public + 143 `private`,
205	  zero carrying `sorryAx`; statement-level, 1560 declarations across 1567 marks = 1372
206	  public + 188 `private`, of which 34 carry `sorryAx`.**  Only the proof-level zero is a
207	  defect count: a statement-level mark on a `sorry` carrier is legitimate, since it claims
208	  the signature is formalised.  Do not delete those 34.
209	
210	  Read that check's own history before writing another one, because it is the sharpest
211	  cautionary tale in this tree.  Its first version reported three dishonest marks; all
212	  three were artifacts of its regex pairing one node's statement with a *later* node's
213	  proof, and one of them had already been settled correctly, by reading, in a commit
214	  message.  Fixing it exposed **six** separate ways it had been silently examining a
215	  strict subset of its domain while printing a clean-looking result — and the last three
216	  were found only because the corrected version *asserts* that
217	  `public + private + unresolved == pins` and the assertion failed.  The lesson is not
218	  "machines beat reading": it is that a mechanical audit needs an arithmetic identity it
219	  must satisfy, checked in code, or "it printed 0 defects" means only that it printed.
220	
221	  Two sharper lessons came out of correcting the correction, and both generalise past
222	  `\leanok`.  The statement-level count above stood as "eleven" for two revisions, and
223	  eleven was *precisely* the intersection with the probe's own output — the very artifact
224	  the paragraph above retracts, still live one paragraph below its own retraction.  So a
225	  domain bug is not fixed when its instance is: every other figure derived by the same
226	  route needs the same identity.  And the 143 `private` pins were published twice as
227	  undecidable, which is true of `#print axioms` and false of `Lean.collectAxioms`; all
228	  1073 are decided, with a positive control to show the private lane is not vacuously
229	  clean.  "My probe cannot see it" is a fact about the probe.
230	- [`blueprint/web/index.html`](blueprint/web/index.html): generated mathematical blueprint.
231	- [`analogies/README.md`](analogies/README.md): index to the historical design notes.
232	- [`../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md):
233	  the alternative Rebuild route.
234	
235	## Layout
236	
237	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/`: sheaf cohomology, the finite-cover Čech
238	  complex, higher direct images, and flat base change.
239	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/`: line bundles, relative Spec, the relative Picard
240	  functor, Grassmannians, Quot schemes, flattening stratification, and Picard
241	  identity components.
242	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/`: rigidity and extension of rational maps, plus the
243	  Albanese factorization.
244	- `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/`: divisor and adelic Riemann–Roch infrastructure.
245	- `blueprint/src/chapters/`: the mathematical blueprint.
246	- `hgraph/`: the generated statement/declaration dependency graph.
247	- `scripts/`: import-minimization and budget-trimming helpers (`min-imports.sh`,
248	  `deumbrella.sh`, `deumbrella-wave.sh`, `trim-budgets.sh`).  They drive
249	  `lake env lean`, never `lake build`, so they do not invalidate the build tree.
250	- `informal/`, `memory/`, `analogies/`: campaign plans, durable notes, and
251	  historical design notes.  See each directory's own index.
252	- [`../../references/summary.md`](../../references/summary.md): shared source
253	  bibliography and retrieval notes.
254	
255	## Build
256	
257	Lean and Mathlib are both pinned at `v4.31.0`.
258	
259	```bash
260	lake exe cache get
261	lake build
262	```
263	
264	For faithful checks, prefer the configured module target.  `lake env lean <file>`
265	does not apply every option from the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` — in particular
266	`maxSynthPendingDepth` — so a direct-file-only instance-synthesis failure can be an
267	option mismatch rather than a source regression.  Files that rely on that option
268	carry a local `set_option` so direct-file, LSP, and module checks agree.
269	
270	This project is part of an Archon Horizon workspace.  Roadmap, task, inbox, and
271	cross-project state live at the workspace root and are reached through the
272	`horizon` CLI.

sheafification is Kleiman's own object; its sheaf property is *proved* in

Be precise about what the wiring buys, because "invoked upstream" is not "proved
upstream". The witness reaches **five** open obligations:

1. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` — representability of the étale-sheafified functor

measures axiom-clean: `Pic0Et.grpObj`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible`,
`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0Et.isSeparated`.

5	## Project
6	
7	A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
8	proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
9	Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
10	smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.
11	
12	This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
13	and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
14	irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
15	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
16	**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
17	(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
18	`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.
19	
20	It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
21	infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
22	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
23	copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
24	which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).

29	  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.

class HasPicSchemeEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : Prop where
  has_pic_scheme_et : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))),

owner decision of 2026-07-28. Its mathematics is

representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor.
